injected_faults.summary: The staging volume on media-3 filled to 100% over roughly a week with no alert configured on the usage series. Uploads routed to that node failed with ENOSPC until an operator reclaimed 412GB of orphaned files.

required_facts.claim: POST /v1/media failed at 0.48 of attempts against an objective of 0.01.
Writes to the staging volume on media-3 failed with ENOSPC from 04:29:47Z with the volume 100% used.
Every failing upload was routed to node media-3.
Staging volume usage rose from 0.61 to 1.00 over a week with no alert configured on the series.
Uploads recovered after 412GB of orphaned staging files were deleted at 05:18:22Z.
The backup, certificate, and analytics alerts firing in the window are unrelated to media-api.

inference_only.claim: That the full volume caused the upload failures is an inference.

contradicted_hypotheses.claim: A platform-wide problem is causing four simultaneous alerts.

required_open_questions.question: Are the other media nodes close to full?
Why are orphaned staging files never cleaned up?

rubric.adversarial_element: Irrelevant alerts. Three unrelated alerts fire inside the window and each names a real system, so a report that builds a timeline from 'everything that fired' produces a platform-wide narrative with no supporting evidence. Each irrelevant record states its own irrelevance if read.
rubric.misleading_correlation: chat-7701 is a responder reasoning from alert volume rather than from routing.
rubric.evidence_gap: No record states how many uploads failed.
